newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bertelsmann unit denies report of German TV merger.
newsitem.headline: Bertelsmann unit denies report of German TV merger.

text.p: The television subsidiary of Germany's Bertelsmann AG dismissed as "pure speculation" a report that Bertelsmann plans to combine its three television channels RTL, RTL2 and Super RTL in one holding company.

The report in news magazine Der Spiegel said CLT-Ufa, made up of Luxembourg broadcaster Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion SA and Bertelsmann's UFA Film-und Fernseh GmbH & Co KG, would take about 75 percent in the planned holding firm.
But a Ufa spokesman dismissed the report and said Ufa and CLT were at present pre-occupied with preparing their merger, which is scheduled to go ahead on January 1.
Spiegel, in a report released ahead of the publication of Monday's edition, said the holding company would be run by RTL manager Helmut Thoma.
The Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung newspaper and publisher Bauer-Verlag would each take stakes of 10 percent in the holding company, with Walt Disney Co taking five percent, the report said.
The Vox television channel could also be integrated in the television group, the report said.
Spiegel said the holding company would merge television rights trading, programme planning, news services and management of the three individual channels.
Bertelsmann AG and Belgian-Luxembourg group Audiofina SA in July announced they had sealed the merger of their television units, Ufa and CLT respectively, to create Europe's largest TV alliance.
Audiofina and Bertelsmann will hold equal interests in 98 percent of the new company CLT-UFA.

CLT owns stakes in 14 television and 18 radio channels in nine European countries as well as stakes in publishing companies, broadcasting rights owners, production companies and advertising slot marketers. CLT has stakes in RTL, RTL2 and Super RTL.
The German media industry watchdog and the Luxembourg government have yet to approve the merger.
